To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the peptide transporters are upregulated by the Janus-Activated Kinase JAK-2, which is known to be involved in tumor growth and metastasis.
JAK2 is a novel regulator of the peptide transport systems PEPT1 and 2.
JAK2 contributes the activity of the peptide transport PEPT1 and to a smaller extent PEPT2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of peptide transporters PEPEPT1 and PEPEPT2 by Janu-activated kinase- 2 (JAK2).
the role of JAK2 in regulating the electrogenic peptide transport in intestine and tumors.
the regulation of the electrogenic peptide transport system PEPT1 and its homolog PEPT2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the JAK/STAT pathway is involved in the regulation of the peptide transport system PEPT1 and/or PEPT2, and that JAK/STAT activation is required for the insertion of the PEPT1 and the PEPT2 transporters into the plasma membrane of the cells.
JAK2 is a regulator of PEPT1 activity, but not of PEPT2 activity, and that the regulation of PEPEPT1 activity by JAK2 involves the regulation of PEPI1 insertion into the cell membrane.
the JAK-STAT pathway is involved in the regulation of peptide transport.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Janus-Activated Kinase-2 JAK-2 is involved in the upregulation of the electrogenic peptide transport systems PEPT1 and 2.
JAK2 is an important regulator of the peptide transporter PEPT1 and that the peptide transporter PEPTS is an important regulator for JAK2.
the peptide transporter PEPT1 is upregulated by Janus kinase JAK2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
JAK2 is involved in the regulation of the peptide transport system.
JAK2 contributes significantly to the regulation of intestinal and renal peptide transport.
JAK2 contributes not only to cancer progression but also to the uptake of nutrients into tumor cells.
